Underside corrosion on rockers, floor pans, jack points and brake/fuel lines (New England car).
Cooling system: pressure test, expansion tank and radiator neck, water pump play, hoses, fan clutch.
S52 VANOS: cold-start rattle and fault codes.
Oil leaks at the valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket and oil pan.
Coilover condition: leaking dampers, top-mount wear, ride height, alignment specs, rear shock mounts.
Rear trailing-arm bushings and the differential mount.
Clutch engagement point, slip test, and transmission/engine mounts.
Intake install and MAF/codes, plus a CA smog-readiness scan (monitors ready, no codes).
Convertible top operation and hydraulics; window regulators; cluster pixels; A/C function.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a VIN with a clean history report, plus trunk-floor/underside photos or a specialist PPI showing an intact (ideally reinforced) rear structure and a sound underside.
Up: receipts for cooling-system renewal and prior-owner maintenance, plus tire date codes within about five years.
Up: a PPI arranged before money moves, and confirmation the original airbox is present for CA smog.
Down: any cracking or tearing at the diff mount or trunk floor, meaningful underside rust, or evidence of track use and abuse.
Down: a refusal to provide the VIN or allow a PPI, or VANOS/cooling faults found at inspection.
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper it is the right variant (S52, manual) at a price that preserves cash. However, it is a modified, undocumented example rather than the stock, well-recorded car a keeper purchase is supposed to justify, and its keeper value hinges on the rear structure and cooling evidence.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2000 M Roadster with a manual gearbox, black over black, at a photographed 107,557 miles. That mileage is consistent with the seller's claim of buying it in 2020 at 94,870. Photos show a clean-looking engine-bay top, an uncracked dash, a tidy soft top and correct staggered Continental tires. They also show several modifications: HS Power coilovers with camber plates, a Racing Dynamics strut bar, an aftermarket intake with an oiled filter, halo projector headlights with visible internal haze, and an Alpine/satellite audio setup. Title status and the work list (fluids, top cylinder, seat bushings, rear windows) are seller claims with no receipts, and there is no VIN. The model's critical items remain open: there is no rear subframe or trunk-floor evidence, no cooling-system history, and nothing on underside corrosion for a Maine car. The S54 rod-bearing concern does not apply to this S52 car. The $11,500 asking price is below the $13,430-$18,081 fair-value band, but the gap coincides with high mileage, non-stock parts and missing documentation.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a title photo, trunk-floor and underside photos, tire DOT codes, and the intake's EO status, and ask whether a PPI at a BMW independent near Eliot, ME is permitted before any deposit.
